newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Ups and downs of latest Middle East peacemaking.
newsitem.headline: Ups and downs of latest Middle East peacemaking.

text.p: Here are some of the key events in Arab-Israeli peace efforts since Benjamin Netanyahu's election as Israel's prime minister 14 months ago:
May 29, 1996 - Right-wing Netanyahu ousts Nobel peace laureate Shimon Peres, vowing to boost Israeli security following wave of suicide bombings that kill 59 people.
July 24 - U.S. President Bill Clinton's Middle East envoy Dennis Ross makes peace trip to Damascus in failed bid to revive Israeli-Syrian talks.
Sept 25 - Violence claiming lives of 61 Arabs and 15 Israeli soldiers erupts over Netanyahu's punching a second entrance into an archaeological tunnel site near Moslem shrines in Jerusalem.
Oct 6 - Following a White House emergency summit, Israel and PLO launch weeks of marathon talks on redeployment from West Bank town of Hebron.
Jan 1, 1997 - Off-duty Israeli soldier Noam Friedman fires into Arab market in Hebron, wounding seven Palestinians in what he says is a bid to sabotage handover.
Jan 17 - Israeli soldiers hand over 80 percent of Hebron, ending 30 years of occupation and formally dividing the volatile town between Arab and Jewish rule.
March 7 - Israeli cabinet approves handover of more of the West Bank to self-rule but Palestinians voice disappointment they are to get only a third of what they had expected.
March 18 - Israel defies world opinion by breaking ground for the Jewish settlement of Har Homa on a hilltop Palestinians know as Jabal Abu Ghneim at edge of Arab East Jerusalem.
March 21 - A bomb in a Tel Aviv cafe kills Palestinian attacker and three Israeli women and wounds 42.
April 4 - Netanyahu offers a Camp David-style meeting with U.S. and Palestinian leaders to close a final peace accord. Palestinians call it a ploy to avoid carrying out interim deals.
April 16 - Europeans arrange a meeting between PLO leader Yasser Arafat and Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy in Malta.
June 27 - Israeli woman pastes posters on shop windows in Hebron depicting Moslem Prophet Mohammad as a pig, triggering outburst of Israeli-Palestinian street battles.
July 16 - Israel demands arrest of Palestinian officers suspected of plotting and ordering attacks on Israelis.
July 23 - Arafat and Levy emerge from meeting in Brussels speaking of significant and positive peace steps.
July 24 - Netanyahu vows to fight plan approved by Israel's Jerusalem municipality to build another Jewish settler enclave in East Jerusalem neighbourhood of Ras al-Amoud.
July 28 - Israel and the PLO agree to resume talks on meeting commitments made under their interim peace deals.
July 30 - Ross postpones peacemaking trip to Middle East because of Jerusalem attack in which two suicide bombers kill 11 people in a Jewish street market.
